question: Who among the following Mauryan king fasted to death and died at Shravanabelagola?
solution:
The Correct Answer is **Chandragupta Maurya.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Chandragupta** lived as an ascetic at **Shravanabelagola** for several years before fasting to death as per the practice of sallekhana, according to the Digambara legend.
 
• **Chandragupta** was the founder of the **Mauryan dynasty **(reigned c. 321–c. 297 BCE) and the first emperor to unify most of India under one administration.
 
• He is credited with saving the country from maladministration and freeing it from foreign domination.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

**Bindusara - **

 
• Bindusara, also known as Bindusara Maurya, was the 2nd Mauryan emperor, who seized the throne in 297 BCE.
 
• He was a Greek Amitrochates (b.c 320 BCE—died 272/3 BCE).
 
• According to Greek historians, he was known as Amitrochates, which is derived from the Sanskrit word amitraghata, which means “destroyer of opponents.”

**Dasharatha - **

 
• Dasaratha Maurya, grandson of Ashoka the Great, ruled as the fourth emperor of the Mauryan Empire from 232 BCE to 224 BCE. Here's a detailed breakdown of his reign:
 
• **Background:**
 
 
• Ascended the throne after his grandfather, Ashoka.
 
• Unlike Ashoka, who was known for his military conquests before embracing Buddhism, Dasaratha's reign is associated with the decline of the Mauryan Empire.
 
 
 
• **Challenges during his reign:**
 
 
• Loss of Territories: Several regions of the vast Mauryan Empire declared independence during Dasaratha's rule. This weakened the empire's central authority.
 
• Limited Ability: Historians believe Dasaratha may not have possessed the strong leadership qualities needed to hold the empire together.
 
 
 
• **Positive aspects:**
 
 
• Continued Ashoka's Policies: Dasaratha is known for upholding the social and religious policies established by his grandfather, particularly the promotion of Dharma (righteousness) and non-violence.
 
• Patronage of Ajivikas: Inscriptions in the Barabar Caves suggest Dasaratha may have patronized the Ajivika sect, a non-vedic philosophical tradition that existed alongside Buddhism during that period.
 
 
 
• **Legacy:**
 
 
• Dasaratha's reign is considered a turning point in Mauryan history. The decline of the empire that began under him continued in the following years.
 
• He was the last Mauryan emperor to leave behind epigraphical evidence (inscriptions) of his rule.
 
• Dasaratha's successor was his cousin, Samprati, who attempted to revive the empire.
 
 
 
• **Ashoka - **
 
 
• Ashoka the Great (r. 268-232 BCE) was the third king of the Mauryan Empire (322-185 BCE)
 
• He is best known for his renunciation of war, development of the concept of dhamma (pious social conduct), and promotion of Buddhism as well as his effective reign of a nearly pan-Indian political entity.
